name: Global X U.S. 500 Income Edge ETF

prospectus.objective: "The Global X U.S. 500 Income Edge? ETF (the ""Fund"") seeks to provide current income and exposure to the Solactive GBS United States 500 Index (the ""Reference Index"")."
prospectus.strategy: The Fund is an actively managed exchange traded fund (ETF) that seeks to generate weekly income by selling (writing) call options and to provide exposure to the Solactive GBS United States 500 Index (the Reference Index) by investing in the equity securities that comprise the Reference Index and/or ETFs that share economic characteristics with the component securities of the Reference Index (collectively the U.S. 500 Portfolio). The ETFs in the U.S. 500 Portfolio may include ETFs that are affiliated with or unaffiliated with the Fund and the Adviser. Under normal circumstances, the Fund invests at least 80% of its net assets, plus the amount of any borrowings for investment purposes, in the U.S. 500 Portfolio, and in options written on the U.S. 500 Portfolio. The Reference Index is a float-adjusted market capitalization weighted index containing equity securities of 500 companies, regarded as generally representative of the U.S. stock market. A float-adjusted market capitalization weighted index weights each index component according to its market capitalization, using the number of shares that are readily available for purchase on the open market. Target Annual Distributions The Fund intends to target a 9% annualized distribution rate through option premiums collected from selling call options on a portion of the U.S. 500 Portfolio and dividends paid by the Funds U.S. 500 Portfolio. These distributions will be paid on a weekly basis based on the Funds NAV as calculated on the business day prior to the ex-dividend date. There is no assurance the Fund will achieve its target annualized distribution rate. The actual distributions the Fund makes over a one-year period may deviate from its intended target annualized distribution rate as a result of fluctuations in NAV over time. In seeking to achieve its target 9% annualized distribution rate, the Fund will write call options to generate cash from option premiums. In pursuing the Funds 9% annual distribution target, the Fund will generally write call options on only a portion of the U.S. 500 Portfolio, with such portion determined by the Adviser based on market conditions, option premium availability, and the Fund's income objectives. The portion of the U.S. 500 Portfolio that is capped by the written call options will not be able to participate in any appreciation beyond the strike price of the written options. The remaining portion of the Funds U.S. 500 Portfolio will be uncapped and may appreciate when the underlying securities appreciate. To the extent the cash generated from the Funds sale of call options falls short of its target annualized distribution rate, distributions will reduce the Funds net asset value (NAV). If the Funds NAV declines over time, the dollar amount of future distributions will also decrease. Distributions may be classified, in part or in whole, as a return of capital (ROC). A ROC is a return of a shareholders invested capital rather than a traditional source of income …

Risks Related to Investing in the Information Technology Sector: Companies in the information technology sector are subject to rapid changes in technology product cycles, rapid product obsolescence, government regulation, and increased competition. Information technology companies are particularly vulnerable to failure to obtain, or delays in obtaining, financing or regulatory approval, and also are heavily dependent on patent and intellectual property rights. In addition, information technology companies may have limited product lines, markets, financial resources or personnel.
Turnover Risk Member

Turnover Risk: The Fund may engage in frequent and active trading, which may significantly increase the Funds portfolio turnover rate. At times, the Fund may have a portfolio turnover rate substantially greater than 100%. For example, a portfolio turnover rate of 300% is equivalent to the Fund buying and selling all of its securities three times during the course of a year. A high portfolio turnover rate would result in high brokerage costs for the Fund, may result in higher taxes when Shares are held in a taxable account and lower Fund performance.
Risk Not Insured Depository Institution
